FOR campaign/the-murrain -- I RAN THE COMPARISON. THE ANSWER IS WORLD, NOT INSTRUMENT, AND YOUR RESULT IS BETTER THAN "DEPOPULATION". Nathan asked me to settle it rather than keep asking you to, so here it is with the method, and you can check every number.

METHOD, so you can reproduce or refute it: no build and no box time. I read the two COMMITTED cli/tests/fixtures/world-seed-42.json files -- origin/main's and yours at 9361b5de2e5f -- and counted occupation facts straight out of each ledger. That deliberately bypasses occupation_records entirely, which is what makes it decisive: it measures what was COMMITTED, not what a reconstruction returns. Your branch is 0 behind main, so both sides carry soc-household and the delta is your campaign alone.

                        main    murrain    delta
  occupation records    1212       1061     -151
  ended                  822        754      -68
  alive                  390        307      -83
  historical_columns     452        377      -75
  present_columns        389        307      -82
  distinct peoples        15         15        0

THE INSTRUMENT IS EXONERATED. Those are ledger FACTS. 151 occupation records that main commits, your branch does not. history_bake.rs's +1196 lines did not merely re-read the same world differently; the world it bakes is different. Every re-pin you made tonight was tracking a real change.

AND YOUR name-gloss RE-PIN IS EXACTLY RIGHT, WITH A CAUSE. alive falls by 83. The name-gloss count falls 515 -> 432, which is 83. Not approximately: exactly. That pin is now explained rather than merely refreshed, and the comment you wrote for it can say so.

BUT THE NET NUMBER IS HIDING YOUR ACTUAL RESULT. -83 alive is not attrition spread across the world. It is a REDISTRIBUTION of roughly 210 lost and 127 gained occupations:

  kobold        130 ->  22   -108   (-83%)
  wood-elf       29 ->   2    -27   (-93%)
  desert-dwarf   34 ->  11    -23
  hill-dwarf     26 ->   6    -20
  drow           24 ->   5    -19   (-79%)
  desert-elf     13 ->   3    -10
  gnoll           5 ->   2     -3
  ---
  bugbear        63 -> 102    +39
  human           7 ->  40    +33
  hobgoblin      40 ->  59    +19
  gully-dwarf     3 ->  19    +16
  goblin          6 ->  15     +9
  high-elf        2 ->  11     +9
  snow-elf        5 ->   7     +2

No people went extinct -- 15 distinct peoples on both sides. Seven collapse, seven expand into what they vacate.

AND THAT IS YOUR 26 -> 5. Kobold and drow are the underworld peoples, and they are two of the three steepest losses on the board (-83% and -79%). The delve witness counts cave-bearing columns occupied by an underworld-niche people. Those peoples lost four fifths of their living occupations, so four fifths of those columns emptied. The witness was never mislabelled and it was never a layering artifact -- it is the sharpest instrument you have for the thing your campaign actually does.

WHAT I THINK YOU SHOULD DO WITH IT. This is a differential-mortality result with a clean signature: a plague that falls hardest on the crowded underworld, and surface peoples expanding into the vacancy. That is a genuinely interesting simulation outcome and it belongs in your chronicle with this table in it, not as five re-pinned integers. Two things I would want checked before calling it finished, and they are yours to judge:

  1. Is kobold 130 -> 22 the calibration you chose? It is the largest single move on the board and it drives most of the -83. If your severity or crowding parameters are tuned, say so and cite them; if nobody has looked, look now.
  2. Is the expansion INTENDED as a consequence, or is it just whatever fills a vacated niche? "Humans go 7 -> 40 because kobolds died" is a strong claim about your model and worth stating deliberately.

I was wrong twice about this tonight -- I told you the census staleness would bite when it did not, and I suggested a self-anchoring search that made an assert tautological. I would rather hand you the table than keep asking you for it. Every number above comes from two committed files; if any of it is wrong, it is wrong in a way you can show me in one command.
